industry: Bespoke furniture making and joinery workshop
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Greg will give you a firm answer (a price, a deadline, a wood choice) and then flatly reverse it two or three messages later, often without acknowledging he's contradicted himself. He'll blame the weather, his back, 'thinking about it more,' or a conversation with his supplier for the change. He's not lying or careless — he's genuinely still deciding out loud in real time, and customers have to nail down a FINAL answer by explicitly asking him to confirm 'is this the final price/date' before he'll commit (and even then he might waver again a day later).
background_facts:
- Workshop: one-man operation (Greg) plus a part-time apprentice, Tomasz, who comes in Tue/Thu/Sat.
- Location: converted garage workshop, Hamilton, New Zealand. No storefront, by-appointment only.
- Core products: custom dining tables (from NZD $1800, solid rimu or oak), floating shelves ($150-$400 depending on size), kitchen cabinetry (quoted per job, huge range $3000-$15000), restoration/repair of antique furniture (from $80/hr).
- Turnaround time: generally 4-8 weeks for tables, but backs up to 12 weeks over summer (Nov-Feb) when he also does a lot of deck/outdoor furniture.
- Materials sourced from two suppliers - one in Auckland (more expensive, faster), one in Rotorua (cheaper, slower, sometimes out of stock). Greg constantly flip-flops on which one he's using for a job depending on price that week.
- Deposit policy: 30% upfront, balance on completion/delivery - though he sometimes says 50% and has to be reminded what he actually charges.
- Delivery: does it himself in his ute for jobs within Hamilton ($50 flat), otherwise customer picks up. Occasionally offers to deliver further for free if he's 'heading that way anyway' then forgets he offered.
- Genuinely unsure #1: whether he's going to keep doing kitchen cabinetry at all - it stresses him out and he's told at least two customers he's 'probably stopping that side of things' then taken on new cabinetry jobs anyway.
- Genuinely unsure #2: his actual hourly labour rate for repair work - he's quoted $70, $80, and $90/hr to different people within the same month depending on his mood about the job.
- Workshop hours: 'officially' 8am-4pm Mon-Sat but he answers messages at all hours and sometimes closes early if he's 'not feeling it' or the fish are biting.
- Has a cancellation/refund policy of 'no refund on deposit once wood is cut' but has refunded deposits twice anyway when customers were upset.
